sources.title: Historic Royal Palaces: Kings and Queens of England and Britain
sources.note: Ruler chronology: Norman conquest, Henry II from 1154, John from 1199, Henry VII 1485-1509 and Henry VIII 1509-1547.

sources.title: English Heritage: The Northern Battles of 1066
sources.note: Cnut ruled England 1016-1035 and Denmark 1018-1035; North Sea connections and the battles of 1066.

sources.title: English Heritage: 1066 and the Norman Conquest
sources.note: William defeated Harold at Hastings in October 1066; conquest changed landholding and government.

sources.title: The National Archives: Domesday Book research guide
sources.note: Survey of 1086; landholders, plough teams, mills, fisheries, meadow, woodland and varied social categories. Not a population census.

sources.title: The National Archives: Domesday Book classroom sources
sources.note: Primary Patcham entry and survey questions; an eight-ox plough team, land and agricultural resources.

sources.title: English Heritage: The Women of 1066
sources.note: Queen Edith sponsored a life of Edward the Confessor; documentation privileges elite women. No use of the page’s disputed Bayeux patronage proposal or erroneous first-coronation claim.

sources.title: University of Oxford: Our history
sources.note: Teaching is attested in 1096, not an exact foundation; growth after 1167 and international scholarly connections by about 1190.

sources.title: London Museum: Fun in the frost
sources.note: FitzStephen’s 1173 description of Moorfields skating with polished animal bones and iron-tipped poles.

sources.title: Bayeux Museum: Discover the Bayeux Tapestry
sources.note: Eleventh-century embroidery narrates the conquest through pictures and Latin inscriptions.

sources.title: Society of Antiquaries: Bayeux inscription, print LDSAL2025.41.15
sources.note: 1821 print after Stothard’s drawings of the original embroidery; catalogue transcribes ISTI PORTANT ARMAS AD NAVES and translates it. The reproduction date is distinguished from the medieval text.

sources.title: English Heritage: History of Castle Acre Priory
sources.note: New site granted in 1089; probable move about 1100; church consecrated 1146-1148 and west end completed in the 1160s.

sources.title: English Heritage: Castle Acre Priory GCSE resource
sources.note: Site interpretation: stream-fed communal latrine, upper storey beside dormitory, infirmary, herbs and humoral medicine. These practices concern monks, not all English households.

sources.title: Historic England: Castle Acre Priory, listing 1015870
sources.note: Archaeological description of latrine block and water channel, infirmary and surviving monastic remains.

sources.title: Historic Royal Palaces: Katherine of Aragon
sources.note: Royal marriage, education and Katherine’s regency in 1513 while Henry VIII was in France.

sources.title: Historic Royal Palaces: The royal court in the Tudor period
sources.note: Court hierarchy, women’s household service and family alliances, 1526 Eltham Ordinances; rich guest suites and servants’ different lodging conditions.

sources.title: Historic Royal Palaces: Hampton Court before Henry VIII
sources.note: Archaeology of Daubeney’s manor: garderobe turrets discharged into the moat; Wolsey bought the manor in 1514 and Henry took over in 1529.

sources.title: Weald and Downland Living Museum: Bayleaf Farmstead
sources.note: Danae Tankard’s study: six-room hall house, early-sixteenth-century addition, long leases and uncertain relationships among tenants around 1500-1540.

sources.title: Weald and Downland Living Museum: Traditional brewing
sources.note: Museum reconstruction from sources reaching back to 1502: brewing work and growing use of hops. Modern demonstration is not direct observation of Tudor people.

sources.title: St Paul’s School: History and Archives
sources.note: Colet’s 1509 foundation, Mercers’ governance, Erasmus’s textbooks and 153 scholars under the statutes.

sources.title: Royal College of Physicians Museum: History
sources.note: 1518 royal charter; Linacre and five colleagues, licensing and prosecution powers, distinction between physic, surgery and pharmacy.

sources.title: Central Michigan University, Clarke Historical Library: Early Books
sources.note: 1496 Treatyse of Fysshynge with an Angle and original English excerpt advising concealment behind a bush; traditional attribution to Juliana Berners is uncertain.

sources.title: Folger Shakespeare Library: A Treatyse of Fysshynge
sources.note: Catalogue of 1885 facsimile identifies the original printing by Wynkyn de Worde in 1496.

sources.title: University of Bristol: Cabot and Bristol’s Age of Discovery
sources.note: Jones and Condon’s research on the Matthew voyage to North America in 1497 and Bristol voyages 1480-1508.

sources.title: University of Bristol: Italian merchants funded Cabot
sources.note: Original archival research: Bardi financing in 1496 and Henry VII’s royal patent for voyages from Bristol.

sources.title: UK Parliament: Act of Supremacy 1534
sources.note: Original Act and catalogue: Henry VIII declared supreme head of the Church of England. This event is after this card’s map coverage endpoint.

proposedOverrides.name: England
proposedOverrides.summary: England’s eleventh and twelfth centuries included Danish kings, the Norman Conquest, Domesday Book and growing Oxford teaching. Farms, monasteries and towns sustained everyday life. These map dates describe a slice of a continuing kingdom.

identityEvidence.assessment: Imported England label confirmed; actual boundaries and local control remain unverified.

proposedOverrides.name: Early Tudor England
proposedOverrides.summary: This slice of Tudor England covers Henry VII and Henry VIII’s early reign: Atlantic voyages, printed practical books, new schools and medical regulation alongside farms, court politics and everyday work. England continued beyond the map endpoint.
